title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing/fairness/starvation prevention/timeouts
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Production traffic has exposed fairness and starvation cases in the continuous-batcher scheduler when there is a long tail of small, low-priority requests coexisting with bursty, high-throughput routes. This PR tunes queueing heuristics, adds aging-based priority adjustments to prevent starvation, and introduces configurable timeouts to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Summary of changes: added queue-weight based scheduling that combines arrival-time aging, request size, and route priority; introduced per-route 'max_queue_time' and global 'fairness_window' knobs; improved timeout handling to proactively evict stale requests and surface retryable errors; added metrics and tracing spans for queue latency, evictions, and fairness score; updated unit and integration tests; added a perf benchmark harness job.

Key behavioral changes (defaults preserved unless configured): - fairness_window_ms (default 200ms): sliding window used to compute per-route served ratios - aging_multiplier (default 1.5): multiplies effective priority for requests waiting longer than fairness_window_ms - max_queue_time_ms (default 1000ms): requests older than this are evicted with a retriable error code and metric "queue_evicted" - head_timeout_ms (default 50ms): maximum time a head request may block batching before triggering speculative dispatch - queue_capacity_soft_limit: when exceeded uses backpressure signals to gateway.

Implementation notes: - Scheduling logic moved into continuous_batcher/scheduler.go with a small, deterministic fair-queue implementation; unit-tested the aging and eviction paths. - KV cache interactions: we ensure KV cache lookups are attempted before eviction where possible; requests with cache hits get increased priority to avoid wasting compute. - Kernel dispatch: scheduler annotates batches with 'latency_budget' hint so the runtime picks narrower-kernel paths for low-latency small-token batches. - Metrics: continuous_batcher.queue_latency_ms (histogram), continuous_batcher.queue_evicted_total, continuous_batcher.fairness_score (gauge per-route), continuous_batcher.speculative_dispatch_count.

Performance results (internal perf-lab, multi-run averages): - 95th percentile latency for small interactive routes: improved from 210ms -> 165ms (~21% lower) - Throughput (tokens/s) at 99th percentile concurrency: unchanged (+/-2%), indicating the fairness adjustments did not harm throughput - Queue evictions: introduced a small number of evictions under pathological backpressure but prevented unbounded latency growth.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind 'continuous_batcher.fair_scheduling' and gated by config defaults. Initial rollout to canary fleet for 48h with latency and evictions alerting enabled, then gradual ramp to all regions over one week.

Related: Linear ENG-5123 (continuous-batcher fairness), ENG-4887 (incident: small-request starvation).

Notes for reviewers: the primary logic is in scheduler.go (~220 LOC) and scheduler_test.go. I focused on correctness and test coverage; open to follow-up perf tuning and parameter name changes.
